commits.message:
fix(taxonomy): writes to canonical_skills.json/job_titles.json were never durable

canonical_skills.json and job_titles.json live inside the git-tracked
source tree (app/understanding/taxonomy/), which `docker compose build`
recreates fresh from git on every deploy. Every write this session
(approving a taxonomy candidate, editing a skill description, the
one-time description backfill) went straight into that git-tracked
path -- meaning into that one container's writable filesystem layer,
which the next unrelated deploy silently discards. Confirmed the hard
way: an entire 181-skill description backfill vanished after the next
deploy for an unrelated fix.

Worse, silently: hermes-api and hermes-graph-consumer are two separate
containers built from the same image, each with its OWN independent
copy of these files in its own filesystem layer. An approval made
through hermes-api's endpoints was never visible to hermes-graph-
consumer -- the process that actually does the async email parsing --
at all, even before the next deploy. Every approved skill/job title
this session may never have actually been recognized by real inbound
mail.

Fixed by moving all reads and writes of these two specific files onto
/hermes-runtime/taxonomy -- the persistent volume already mounted into
both containers (docker-compose.yml, the same one HERMES_ACCESS_
CONTROL_FILE already uses for exactly this kind of runtime-mutable
state). _writable_taxonomy_path() seeds the runtime copy from the git-
tracked baseline on first use in a given environment and is lru_cache'd
so the seed-check only happens once per process; every write after
that goes straight to the shared, persistent copy, which a rebuild
never touches and both containers see identically. skill_aliases.json/
title_aliases.json are untouched -- nothing writes to them, so they
stay plain git-tracked files.

New coverage: a write leaves the git-tracked seed file byte-for-byte
unchanged; the write lands under the runtime directory; a fresh
process's first call (cache cleared, simulating a restart) finds the
existing runtime copy and does not re-seed over it, losing the earlier
write. Full regression suite (18 checks) green.

Immediate follow-up after this deploys: re-run scripts/hermes-taxonomy-
generate-descriptions.py once against the now-persistent path to
restore the 181 descriptions lost to this bug.
